title: 1+4+9 in One Step: Special Series Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
One, plus four, plus nine, plus sixteen: the square numbers. How many tiles for the first ten squares, or the first hundred? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 8, Sequences and Series) we add natural numbers, their squares and their cubes, each in one step.

You will learn the sigma sign, watch square tiles stack up live while every total matches the rule n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, and see why it works: a chain of cubes that cancel in pairs. Then the surprise that the sums of cubes 1, 9, 36, 100 are all perfect squares, a side-by-side of the two formulas, a worked example, the exam trap that mixes up the sum of squares and the square of the sum, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: these special series were removed from the current NCERT Class 11 text, but JEE still asks them.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 One formula for 1 + 4 + 9 + ...
0:27 The sigma sign and the sum of 1 to n
0:51 Live: add one square at a time
1:14 Why the rule works: cubes cancel
1:59 Sums of cubes are perfect squares
2:19 Squares vs cubes side by side
2:55 Worked example: the first 10 squares
3:30 Exam trap: sum of squares vs square of the sum
3:48 Where it is asked
3:59 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:33 Recap and three questions to answer

This completes Chapter 8, Sequences and Series. Every episode is in the PUC Maths | Class 11 playlist.
